title: aggregate-cred-prefetch-and-stream-termination-builder
author: Priya Nandakumar
description: Context: Several customers and internal integrations reported two related friction points across SDKs: (1) a cold-start latency spike when the credential provider path did a blocking lookup on first stream/connection, and (2) inconsistent application-level behavior when streams are terminated from the SDK side (some clients observed resource leaks or orphaned iterator state). Motivation: Reduce first-byte latency for auth-backed streaming calls, provide a single ergonomic builder for graceful stream shutdown and explicit termination hooks, and expose a small surface to specialize retry behavior at the stream-level (rather than only at request-level). This PR introduces a cross-SDK pattern in the redwood repo: an AggregateCredentialPrefetch helper plus a StreamTerminationBuilder. The goal is to offer an opt-in but easy-to-use default that: - eagerly prefetches credentials (non-blocking if configured) during client creation or session start - exposes a fluent builder that composes cancellation, graceful drain, and a mandatory finalizer callback for resource cleanup - allows per-stream retry specialization: maxTokenRetries, backoffProfile, and idempotencyHint Summary of changes: - core/auth: add AggregateCredentialPrefetch interface and a lightweight async prefetch orchestration (Go/Py/TS shim connectors in this repo). Prefetch is opt-in via ClientOptions. - sdk/*: expose StreamTerminationBuilder on the session/stream factory. The builder has methods: .withGracePeriod(ms), .onFinalize(fn), .withRetryHints({maxRetries, profile}), .terminateNow() and .terminateGracefully(). - py/ts/go clients: ergonomic changes to surface the builder on Session.stream() and Client.open_stream(). - tests: add end-to-end streaming tests that simulate credential refresh latency, network flakiness, and verify no goroutine/task/worker leaks after termination. - docs: short QUICKSTART snippet showing the builder and credential prefetch usage. Commits: - 7f12c8a: introduce AggregateCredentialPrefetch interface and core orchestration (initial tests) - 3b4d1f2: add StreamTerminationBuilder API and plumbing into session factories - a8e0f44: python client bindings + examples - d2be4c7: typescript client bindings + iterator ergonomics - 0f9d2ae: go client bindings + concurrency safety fixes - 4c3b9e1: tests for leaking resources and flakiness harness - ec7b1f0: docs and release note draft Files changed (high level): - core/auth/prefetch.go (new) - core/auth/prefetch_test.go (new) - sdk/common/stream_termination_builder.go (new) - sdk/python/redwood/stream_termination.py (updated) - sdk/typescript/src/stream/termination.ts (updated) - sdk/go/client/stream.go (updated) - tests/streaming/credential_prefetch_harness.go (new) - docs/quickstarts/streaming-prefetch.md (new) - examples/streaming/prefetch-example.py (new) Compatibility and ergonomics notes: - The new client option default is OFF for prefetch to avoid surprising behavior for customers with specialized auth flows. We enable an environment variable REDWOOD_SDK_PREFETCH=1 for internal experiments. - StreamTerminationBuilder is additive: existing call sites that use raw iterators continue to work; the builder is returned as an alternative factory method. - Retry specialization is advisory: it is passed to the runtime as a hint; it will not override cluster/global routing policies. Testing and CI: - Local integration harness validated across py/ts/go with the internal flakiness simulator. - CI added matrix runs that exercise termination under short/long grace periods and with/without prefetch. - All checks passed after two re-runs of flaky system tests. Migration and rollout: - Feature flagged behind an opt-in ClientOptions flag. - Documentation and quickstart added. - Release note draft included in release_notes below. Related work: ENG-1402 (reduce auth cold-start latency), ENG-1429 (stream leak detection and fixes). Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed by Maya - [x] End-to-end tests added - [x] SDK bindings implemented for py/ts/go - [x] Docs quickstart added - [x] Release note drafted,
review_thread: Reviewer: Maya Chen - Please add explicit docs about the prefetch failure modes (what happens if the prefetch call errors). Author: Prefetch errors are surfaced via client-level telemetry and do not abort client creation; I added a ClientOption.onPrefetchError callback in the latest patch. Reviewer: Diego Alvarez - Go stream termination had a data race when .terminateGracefully() was called during an active drain; please re-run the race detector. Author: fixed; added mutex and an atomic state enum plus a targeted race test. Diego: approved after the race test passed locally. Reviewer: Liam O'Connor - We need clearer guidance on when to enable prefetch in serverless environments. Author: added note in quickstart and added REDWOOD_SDK_PREFETCH env var for experimentation. CI: system-tests flaky on first run (network simulator), rerun fixed. Approvals: Maya (APPROVED), Diego (APPROVED), Liam (APPROVED). Merge: squash and merge after approvals and green CI.
release_notes: - SDK: Add AggregateCredentialPrefetch opt-in helper to reduce cold-start latency for auth-backed streams. - SDK: Introduce StreamTerminationBuilder to gracefully terminate streams and attach finalizers. - SDK: Allow per-stream retry specialization as advisory hints. Notes: feature is opt-in via ClientOptions and gated by REDWOOD_SDK_PREFETCH for experiments. No breaking changes.
